title: Physical-media fallback and automated rollback requirements for Private/VPC deployments
creator: Sofia Nguyen
description: Background: Customers with fully air-gapped Private/VPC deployments require an auditable, operator-friendly mechanism to receive urgent security patches or CVE fixes when standard networked artifact delivery is unavailable. This ticket defines the product requirements and acceptance criteria for supporting physical-media (USB / customer-provided registry images / signed tarball) intake, verification, staged application, and automated rollback for emergency patch delivery. The intent is not to replace normal remote upgrade flows, but to provide a hardened fallback that preserves zero-egress guarantees and reduces operator toil while meeting compliance/audit expectations.
scope_included: Support for ingesting signed artifacts via operator-provided physical media (USB image or SCP of signed tarball) into the private deployment's image store or local registry.
Cryptographic verification of artifact signatures against a configurable trust chain (customer KMS/HSM or Redwood-supplied root with customer approval).
An operator CLI and Console workflow for: artifact ingestion, dry-run validation, staged canary rollouts (node subset), full rollout, and automated rollback on defined failure criteria.
A minimal offline build of the upgrade orchestrator that can run within air-gapped environments and provide granular progress/audit logs stored locally (and optionally exported).
A documented playbook and runbook for physical media handling (chain-of-custody checklist), plus GPG/PKI signing verification steps for customers and SRE teams.
Automated preflight checks (disk space, kernel/module compatibility, driver ABI checks, runtime health) executed in air-gapped environment prior to applying patch.
scope_excluded: Automatic retrieval of artifacts from internet mirrors on customer's behalf (this ticket does not create outbound egress by default).
New KMS integrations that require cloud-side key escrow; we only support on-prem KMS/HSM or user-uploaded public keys for verification within air-gapped installs.
Replacement of the existing networked upgrade flow for non-emergency/regular releases.
success_criteria: Operators can apply a signed emergency patch using only physical media and local operations within the Private/VPC deployment with no outbound network traffic by default.
Artifact signature verification and provenance metadata is recorded in local audit logs and visible in Console (when Console has connectivity) or in the offline runbook export.
Rollout tooling supports canary on 1-2 nodes, health gating, and automated rollback on <3% error rate or defined operator thresholds.
Post-rollback system state matches pre-patch baseline within defined tolerances (service health/responsiveness), validated by automated health checks and KV cache integrity checks.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Artifact ingestion: A documented operator flow that copies artifacts from physical media to a designated local artifact directory or local registry, with checksum and signature verification producing a signed ingestion record (artifact-id and signature verification result).

2) Signature verification: System verifies signed artifacts against a configurable trust anchor. Test vectors include: Redwood-signed artifact, customer-signed artifact (customer public key uploaded), and an intentionally corrupted artifact that must be rejected.

3) Dry-run validation: CLI command 'ri private patch --dry-run --artifact <id>' runs preflight checks and emits a pass/fail report without making any changes. Dry-run must detect missing disk space, missing vendor kernel modules, incompatible runtime ABI, and return non-zero exit code on failures.

4) Canary rollout: The orchestrator can apply the patch to a subset of nodes (configurable, default=2) and run post-deploy probes (latency, token-per-second, model-serving health). Canary must complete within operator-defined timeout or automatically rollback.

5) Automated rollback: If X% of post-deploy probes fail (default 5%) within Y minutes (default 30m), the system triggers an automated rollback to the recorded pre-patch snapshot with a single CLI/Console action and provides clear progress and failure reasons.

6) Auditability: All steps (ingest, signature verification, dry-run results, rollout events, rollback events) must be appended to a tamper-evident local audit log and include timestamps, operator id, artifact-id, and signed hashes. Logs must be exportable as JSON/CSV.

7) Chain-of-custody playbook: Provide a plain-language checklist and Console CLI output that an operator can follow to demonstrate compliance (who handled media, when, checksums verified). This playbook must be reviewed and approved by Security before roll-out.

8) Zero-egress assurance: By default, no outbound network calls are made during ingest/verify/deploy. Any temporary egress option must be behind an explicit operator flag and require customer approval with an audit trail.
9) KMS verification: Support for verifying signatures using on-prem KMS/HSM public keys (test: customer-provided PKCS#11 public key used to verify a signed artifact).

10) Recovery time objective: Full rollback to baseline must complete within the documented RTO for emergency patch scenarios (target: 45 minutes for median cluster size defined in PrivateDeployOps sizing guide).

11) Operator UX: Console displays a clear, stepwise migration status for the physical-media flow; if Console has no network connectivity to the deployment, equivalent CLI output and local HTML report are produced.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Chain-of-custody failures or lost media could create compliance gaps. Mitigation: provide explicit checklist, mandated operator attestation, and optional secure media transfer HSM support.
Risk: Corrupted or malicious media. Mitigation: mandatory multi-step signature verification and artifact hash checks; reject anything failing verification.
Risk: Unexpected kernel/module incompatibility after patch. Mitigation: enforce dry-run compatibility checks and require snapshot/saved state prior to rollout; fail-safe automated rollback.
Risk: Operators mistakenly enabling temporary egress. Mitigation: require two-person approval for enabling egress; flag and audit trail logged.
